Indian Standard ( Part II ) was adopted Standards Institution on 30 March 1979, after the draft Shipbuilding Sectional Committee had been approved Cargo Movement and Packaging Division Council.

0.2 Adoption of too severe tolerances for acceptance of screw propellers may result in increased manufacturing cost with no corresponding increase in the performance of the finished propeller. Therefore, there is a need for a range of propeller tolerances which are .expected to produce satisfactory results, depending upon the operation of various kinds of propellers. 0.3 This standard is based on ISO/DIS 484( Part I )-I977 Shipbuilding Ship_scrlr; propellers - Manufacturing tolerances for casting and finish. - Propellers of diameter greater than 2'5 metre, issued by :iE International Organization for Standardization ( IS0 ). 0.4 This standard is one of a series of Indian Standards propellers. Other standards in the series are: on ships' screw

4.5 Location of Blades, Location of Reference Lines and of Blade contours 4.5.1 Marking of Lines of Reference - The reference line is a straight line shown on the drawing and passing through a point Mon the This point M should be marked on a cylindpressure side of the blade. rical section at a radius greater than O-5 R and, if possible, in the region of O-7 R. It is in principle selected in such a way that the line OM cuts the largest possible number of blade sections.
